loading_eclipse_gameplay_1: Standing still helps control your recoil and improve your accuracy. Crouching further enhances the effect.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_2: A Medic Bag restores only one down per use.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_3: There is a maximum of 100 skill points to spend in Eclipse.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_4: Firing an unsuppressed weapon at an enemy may cause them to lose accuracy, take cover, avoid you, or outright panic.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_5: Hostages can be traded during assault breaks to restore a single down.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_6: A cunning Crew Chief has the ability to negotiate better terms during Hostage Trades.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_7: Work together and work quickly, as with every subsequent Assault Wave the enemy will arrive better armed and more determined to take you down.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_8: Sentry Guns can be used as a distraction while moving across an open area.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_9: Getting shot at delays your armor regeneration—consider returning fire to discourage any harrassers.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_10: Starting a heist in stealth and then finishing it loud is a valid strategy.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_11: Shotguns deal damage per pellet—so you must be close enough for most pellets to hit to inflict full damage.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_12: Spycams can spot Special Enemies during loud approach.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_13: Playing aggressively is not always the answer.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_14: Placing a Sentry Gun on head- or torso-level cover lets it land headshots more consistently.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_15: Protect your teammates from cover whenever they move through an open area or interact with an objective.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_16: Taking hostages can slow down cop advances.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_17: Inspiring a teammate gives them resistance to armor suppression.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_18: Shields are highly resistant to explosions from the front.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_19: Staying in one spot for too long may prompt cops to deploy tear gas.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_20: You lose a small amount of stamina each time you’re hit by enemy fire.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_21: Full Force Onslaught is a part of the Pro Job modifier—which activates during escape sequences on most heists; it drastically ups the difficulty by introducing improved enemy groups with new tactics and increased enemy presence.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_22: Friendly Fire is enabled during Pro Jobs.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_23: Shields will work together with other units by actively providing them with cover and harrassing heisters.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_24: Eclipse difficulty introduces an Elite Marksman to the assault force—a ground Sniper unit that's deployed with other SWATs.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_25: Some cops remain behind during assault breaks to cover retreating forces and stop heisters from fleeing.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_26: Cops will announce their retreats early, giving you a good indication of when to start focusing on your escape or your objectives.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_27: Cloakers are silent on Eclipse difficulty.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_29: Staying in Casing Mode during stealth helps you locate objectives for masked teammates or slip past guards yourself.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_30: Some doors can be shot open at the handle or blown open with explosives.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_31: Escaping during an ongoing police assault has a higher chance of triggering an Escape Day if you don’t have the Expert Driver asset
loading_eclipse_gameplay_32: Stay in cover as often and as long as possible.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_33: Consider funneling cops along specific paths to make them easier to eliminate or to gather ammo.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_34: Infamy doesn’t reduce skill-tier requirements in Eclipse.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_35: Avoid placing all your team’s deployables in the same spot.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_36: Cops prioritize attacking vulnerable heisters—for example, when they’re reloading or interacting with objects.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_37: Eclipse difficulty introduces an Elite Shield to the assault force—his shield is immune to piercing ammo and knockback, but breaks under sustained fire.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_38: Melee weapons can deal headshot damage. Blunt melee weapons deal more headshot damage than sharp ones.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_39: With each assault wave, cops use smoke bombs and flashbangs more aggressively.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_40: Killing civilians during a Pro Job heist will increase the difficulty of police assaults.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_41: The Grinder perk deck converts all your armor into health, allowing you to use any armor type and still regenerate health by dealing damage.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_42: The Gambler perk deck lets you regain health and share ammo pickups with your team without any cooldowns.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_43: Your aim is much worse when shooting on the move with an LMG.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_44: LMGs and some special weapons slow you down when equipped.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_45: You take less damage when using a vehicle.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_46: Try skills, weapons, or perks you’ve rarely used—you might discover a new favorite or a new role on your team.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_47: Destroying a camera will cause a guard to investigate.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_48: Enemy snipers become very inaccurate when actively shot at.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_49: Suppressors prevent shots from attracting attention and make enemies less likely to dodge.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_50: Headshot Fury replaces Graze, rewarding accuracy by increasing headshot damage with each consecutive headshot.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_51: Refill your resources from deployed equipment before moving to a new area.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_52: Most heists allow a free alternate escape method if done in stealth.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_53: Saws have a passive damage multiplier against Bulldozers.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_54: Bullets and slugs deal reduced damage when penetrating enemies, walls, or shields.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_55: Light SWAT units carrying SMGs can suppress heisters more effectively over distance and be very deadly up close.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_56: Bulldozers constantly harass heisters and are reluctant to retreat during assault breaks.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_57: Bulldozers usually come along with a team of other heavy units to assist them.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_58: During assault break recon, HRT is often assisted by Cloakers or Tasers to disrupt heisters.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_59: Eclipse difficulty introduces several exclusive elite enemy groups, each featuring multiple Special Units working together.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_60: Medics tend to take cover behind other SWAT units in order assist them as much as possible.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_61: Because Hoxton is imprisoned almost weekly—breaking out and crashing into FBI HQ—FBI Boss Agent Riker has finally decided to take matters into his own hands to end this never-ending cycle...
loading_eclipse_gameplay_62: Some heists feature US Army soldiers who fight alongside the assault or guard areas during stealth. Unlike regular cops, they won’t hesitate to take you down.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_63: During some heists, FBI Ready Teams join the assault wave; they’re better trained, better armed, and employ a wider variety of tactics against heisters.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_64: Kiting—running away from cops to lure them to another area of the heist—is a valid strategy.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_65: Enemy HP is based on unit type and faction. Only boss-type enemies have HP that scales with difficulty.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_66: Tear gas bypasses armor, strips stamina, and directly damages health—its damage scales exponentially the longer you’re exposed.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_67: If you’re alone and can’t reach a specific location during an assault, it’s usually better to play it safe and wait it out than get downed in the open.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_68: The Hitman perk deck is an aggressive playstyle that rewards quick, accurate kills.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_69: Cloakers can still charge and dropkick a solo player, initially dealing only health damage. If your health is low enough, the attack can down you.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_70: First Aid Kits only restore a portion of your total health, although they can also be upgraded to grant temporary health regeneration.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_71: A Marksman Rifle is a weapon type that bridges Sniper and Assault Rifles.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_72: Killing cops matters, but focus on staying together and completing the objective—your resources are finite, theirs are not.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_73: During a Pro Job, your down timer decreases each time you go down. Just like in PAYDAY: The Heist.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_74: Stats aren’t everything—low-damage weapons have other advantages that compensate for their weak stopping power.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_75: Eclipse Overhaul’s balance focuses on player skill and team synergy across varied playstyles—not on build-based power fantasies.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_76: Fat cops pack a heavier punch than other cops, because of training.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_77: LMGs, Marksman Rifles and Shotguns are all highly effective at suppressing enemies.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_78: The Pro Job modifier offers a completely new way to play PAYDAY 2.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_79: The Crook perk deck grants damage reduction when you take health damage and immunity to penetrating sniper shots and armor suppression.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_80: The Maniac and Muscle perk decks give you a chance to induce panic in enemies when you shoot.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_81: Armor regeneration time depends on the armor’s weight.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_82: Grace period is shorter the higher the difficulty.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_83: You must be at least level 80 or above to access Eclipse difficulty.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_85: Always stay close to your teammates.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_86: Sentry Guns last longer when used defensively rather than offensively.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_87: The range stat on melee weapons can make a big difference.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_88: Weapon modifications (stats only) are limited to magazines, ammo types, sights, barrels, barrel extensions, and conversion kits—though a few special items are exempt; everything else is purely cosmetic.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_89: Take your time—don’t rush into higher difficulties.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_90: Enemies deal the same damage at all ranges, except shotgunners.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_91: Special weapons—flamethrowers, miniguns, and rocket launchers—have no ammo pickups.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_92: The Sicario smoke bomb grants teammates a large dodge bonus and armor suppression immunity; these effects linger for a few seconds after leaving the smoke.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_93: Sentry guns and damage-over-time effects don’t trigger Grinder HP Regen or Maniac’s Hysteria.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_94: A Bulldozer’s faceplate durability scales with difficulty.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_95: Consider joining the Eclipse Discord server to stay updated, share feedback, or find other players to heist with.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_96: Flamethrowers can penetrate through enemies and shields.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_97: ECM Jammers remain useful during loud phases thanks to their Feedback ability.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_98: Splitting into two groups is risky but effective, forcing enemies to spread out instead of attacking full force.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_99: A grenade’s trajectory is relative to your current movement direction.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_100: Sniper Rifles are loud—making you easier to spot in stealth and drawing more enemy attention in loud. By contrast, SMGs and Pistols are much quieter.
loading_eclipse_gameplay_101: Not all targets are treated equally. Heists in locations of political, economic, or strategic significance are met with a disproportionate law enforcement response.
